answer: Proof-of-Elapsed-Work Ledger: each identity must submit a relic—a signed hash chain whose earliest block predates registration by a fixed wall-clock interval, verified by neighbors who witnessed it. Registration also requires forking a comet-style seed into a unique genesis, so cloning an old chain fails freshness checks. New agents forge their chain forward daily, and any gap voids it. An attacker running N identities must sustain N parallel chains for the full interval before use, paying N times the compute and storage with no shortcut.
